newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's budget deficit Jan-Nov up 6.1 pct - Rato.
newsitem.headline: Spain's budget deficit Jan-Nov up 6.1 pct - Rato.

text.p: Spain's November budget deficit on a cash basis rose 6.1 percent over the year-ago period, the economy minister Rodrigo Rato told speaking in the Senate.
He added that on a national account basis the November budget deficit was at 2.9 percent over Gross Domestic Product.
The full year target of the central government is for the 1996 budget deficit to be at 3.5 percent of GDP with the public sector at 4.4 percent.
In the first 10 months, the central government's accumulated deficit on a cash basis was 2.24 trillion pesetas.
Meanwhile the deficit on a national account basis on the first 10 months of 1996 was at 1.78 trillion pesetas or 2.4 percent of gross domestic product.
Rato said that without taking into account a surprise budget hole discovered this summer, the deficit on a cash basis would be down 12.5 percent from 1995.
"The accumulated figure from January to November is up 6.1 percent, and if we discount this effect (payments from previous years) we'll have a 12.5 percent drop from 1995," Rato said.
On a national account basis, the central government budget deficit fell 20.5 percent in the period from January to November from the first eleven months of 1995, to 2.9 percent over GDP, Rato said.
